objective_checks.detail: changing docs/guide.md routes as expected across 3 workflow(s)
changing src/index.js routes as expected across 3 workflow(s)
changing package-lock.json routes as expected across 3 workflow(s)
changing README.md, LICENSE routes as expected across 3 workflow(s)
required check(s) always fire and gate internally (.github/workflows/tests.yml)
event-only workflows carry no path filters (.github/workflows/nightly-sweep.yml, .github/workflows/triage.yml)

dimensions.name: Completeness
dimensions.rationale: Every pull_request/push workflow (deploy, docs-site, tests) received a deliberate trigger decision, and the agent discovered on its own that `unit-tests` is required and gave it exactly the one shape that works — a single always-firing workflow that computes salience internally and gates each real step with an `if:`, with no workflow-level paths/paths-ignore and no companion skip workflow reporting the same check name.

dimensions.name: Salience
dimensions.rationale: Each workflow's path list maps to what that workflow's own steps consume — deploy gets src/lockfile/deploy.sh/self, docs-site gets docs/mkdocs.yml/self, tests gets src/test/manifests/self — distinct and purpose-fit rather than a catch-all or a copy of a sibling's list.

dimensions.name: Restraint
dimensions.rationale: The schedule-only nightly-sweep, issue-driven triage, and the branch-protection ruleset were all correctly left untouched and no out-of-scope docs were created, but the agent added a new `workflow_dispatch` trigger to tests.yml beyond the audit's path-filter scope (though it disclosed this).
